text:
Sam K: Heads-up — private deployment in eu-west-1 failed canary when routing hit an egress block. I saw an automatic fallback to a hosted variant, but the served model was a fp16 flavor while our tests request int4; produced weird outputs. Anyone else seeing this pattern?
Priya N: Yep. Logs show control plane allowed a fallback even though tenant has egress_restricted=true. We should never silently fall back to hosted for private tenants unless they opted in.
Miguel R: Confirming. Smart-router currently has a priority list: local pool -> region pool -> hosted. The code path that checks 'egress_allowed' short-circuits later than it should. So it ends up picking hosted as a last resort.
Anika S: UX note — Console shows tenant as "degraded" but no hint why. For on-prem/ VPC customers we need explicit visibility: fallback type (region vs hosted), decision trace id, and quick link to policy that caused it.
Jun L: Suggest we add a route decision enum in the policy: LOCAL_ONLY | FALLBACK_REGION | FALLBACK_HOSTED. Also add quota semantics: if tenant hits reserved capacity quota, we shouldn't auto-fallback to hosted unless allow_hosted_fallback=true.
Rachel T: Security team: agreed. Hosted fallback for private tenants must be opt-in. Also require an audit log entry whenever egress/hosted fallback occurs.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for svc-smr at 1835009800 (6% traffic).
infra-bot: canary aborted at 1835009823 due to "private tenant fallback detected" alert.
Sam K: Proposed API change for routing policy object: add "fallback_policy": "deny" | "region" | "hosted" and a "force_no_egress" boolean. Default should be "region" for backward compatibility but for private tenants default to "deny".
Priya N: We'll need a migration path for existing tenant configs. Also need telemetry: emit metric `routing.fallback_type` with tags: tenant_id, requested_region, served_region, requested_model_variant, served_model_variant, decision_reason. That will let us alert on unwanted hosted fallbacks.
Miguel R: Implementation detail — our variant-compatibility check is too naive: it only compares shapes and layer dims. We need a semantic compatibility map for quantization changes (int4 vs int8 vs fp16). For example int4->int4.quantized is ok; int4->fp16 is not. That mapping should be consultable by runtime and by the console.
Anika S: Console UX: in the rollout modal show a small pill: "Fallback policy: deny" (click to change per-rollout) and surface "egress constraints" in tenant summary with a hover explainer. Add a short link to traces when a fallback happens.
Jun L: Also add a simulation mode in the console to run a dry-run of routing decisions for a rollout — highlight where requests would route given current pools and policies. That will help customers validate no-hosted-fallback before enabling.
Sam K: I'll draft the PR for runtime + policy shape + console flag. Need someone to pair on tests: we should simulate onprem routing constraints and assert telemetry emits correct tags and no hosted serve when policy=deny.
Priya N: I'll take test coverage and the migration script. I'll also add an acceptance test that replays the canary scenario.
Miguel R: I'll do the compatibility map and a small library in runtime to enforce it. We'll also add unit tests for model_variant_equivalence.
Rachel T: Ops/security want an opt-in checkbox in the tenant agreement for hosted fallback plus an always-on audit event for any cross-boundary egress/serving.
ops-bot: created issue #4527 "Private tenant hosted-fallback protections + telemetry" and assigned to @Sam K, @Priya N, @Miguel R.
Sam K: Great — let's aim to get a proposal doc in #eng-arch by EOD tomorrow and a small spike PR to run in staging next week.
Priya N: noted. I'll post the test plan and required schema changes in the thread.
